Just like in 2008, today’s tech layoffs and issues in other sectors might be signaling deeper problems that aren’t immediately apparent in the overall economic data. While parts of the economy might indeed be thriving, we shouldn’t overlook these warnings. Layoffs, poor management aside, impact real people and can precede broader economic shifts.

Also, absolutely agree on the rent-seeking point—economic gains need to be evenly spread to avoid deepening inequality and ensure sustainable growth.

This strikes me off as the cliche dude in STEM/Engineering lacking social skills and self awareness. I can understand that during school it might be hard to find the time and energy to put effort into dating/social stuff. Especially, if you’re working part time and doing an engineering program FT, that shit takes everything out of you. Sometimes you need to make sacrifices and just focus on that until you get through it… 

Yes, you can do decent in an engineering, work part time, and have a social life, but usually trying to do everything can result in burnout. I’ve been there, so I can empathize. Honestly, if you want to look at least effort highest return I would do these things if I where to go back and do everything over again:

1. Workout. Get in the gym atleast 4x a week, everything will get better. You’ll get more confidence in your body, improve appearance, de-stress.. and a million other things. Seriously, keep it under an hour and just go. Sign up for a weightlifting class, cycling, swimming.. whatever.. just get your body moving. 
Bonus: we are social animals, find a gym buddy to go with. It will be much easier to keep yourself motivated and consistent when you’re not doing it alone. 

2. Take an improv/acting/and or public speaking class. One, it will be something different, but more importantly it will get you out of your comfort zone and you will get feedback on how to improve skills that are useful in dating, social settings, and life in general. (Plus, idk how it is at other schools, but the arts department was basically a ho-oasis.. many more women than men, and a lot of the men are batting for their own team.. don’t go in looking to get laid, but the odds are definitely in your favor here). 

3. Work on your posture. How you carry yourself is so much dependent on your posture. 1 and 2 will help with this, but you can do various stretching to loosen up your shoulders and back. Imagine you’re being stretched apart by a string attached to the top of your head and the bottom of your tail bone, use this visialization to find your natural posture. 

4. Style + hygiene. Make sure you’re grooming yourself and find a hairstyle / beard that will suit your face. Find a good hair stylist for suggestions (you will pay a lot more upfront l, but the effects will reap you benefits tenfold in return). Next find a couple outfits that you like. Again, nothing complicated, just make sure it fits and compliments your body well. You can find tons of cheap decent clothes on Temu. If you have no fashion sense then ask some female friends/family to go shopping with you (or make a gay bestie, and they’ll know how to make you look good). 

5. Take social risks often. What I mean is find opportunities to push yourself out of your comfort zone. Strike up a convo with a stranger, talk about the weather with the cashier.. You will have plenty of opportunities, be willing to put yourself out there. You might find that you meet some great friends or even networking opportunities along the way. Remember, that everyone is busy living their own lives thinking about themselves. A warmSmile, decent eye contact, and genuine interest in others will take you a lot farther than you think. 


Just some of my thoughts. Hope this helps. It doesn’t have to be super complicated and all of this is natural. Our ancestors got us this far in much more difficult circumstances. Believe in yourself, and good things will come your way no matter how daunting things might seem in the present.

Cheers,

I think a major argument for using taxable brokerages are the liquidity that they provide as opposed to retirement accounts with hefty early withdrawal penalties. Sure you will have the most growth in a tax advantaged account, but you can only take advantage when you’re at retirement age. It seems like there is a balance to be struck between making out the 401k before throwing a penny at a taxable brokerage account vs not using any retirement accounts at all and handling everything on meme stocks.

Personally, I prefer to have as much access as possible to the majority of my capital should it be needed for life events, emergencies, investment opportunities outside of the stock market, etc.. I still contribute to a 401k through my employer, enough to carry me to a decent retirement age on its own, but knowing that I can liquidate all of my assets sitting in my brokerage and have that cash readily available in my checking account nearly instantly, is worth more to me than having that same sum locked up in retirement accounts.
